title: HALO exponents 20, 42, 45, 48 and the normalizer 100 can fall under the ceiling 16 p^2 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/gaussian-halo-exponents/`. It answers the open question of #4403: if both 2-norms are at most `16 p^2`, which of HALO's exponents 20, 42, 45 and 48, and GAUSSIAN's normalizer 100, can decrease?

**Claim type:** conditional exponent arithmetic. **No new κ.** The ceiling is not proved for the rounded reference `H`, and the #4100 notes are not edited.

All five can decrease. For every integer `p >= 2` and every integer bandwidth `W <= p - 1`, the same locality argument with the stronger ceiling gives:

| Written | Replacement |
| --- | ---: |
| 20 | 12 |
| 42 | 26 |
| 45 | 28 |
| 48 | 28 |
| 100 | 7 |

The error is then strictly below `p^6 exp(-p^2)`, and a row at distance `p^28` from a section edge matches the global polynomial row. Each replacement is the smallest uniform integer with that role. The written core exponent 400 remains sufficient and can fall to 86; this package does not retune it.

## Not covered

- Phase cuts, truncation and rounding, so `||H^-1||_2 <= 16 p^2` is not claimed for the rounded matrix.
- An edit to HALO.md, GAUSSIAN.md or PROOF.md. The written exponents stay sufficient.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19102574
